text:
anya: Heads-up - ACME reported a bad mapping between tool results when they invoke two tools in parallel. Customer saw tool A's response attached to tool B's call_id; schema validation then failed downstream.
support-bot: Incident created: INC-7592 (auto). Correlation: r=acme-9f3a. Collecting logs.
kevin: Can you paste the original request and the two tool args? Need request_id and correlation id.
anya: request_id=rdw-req-20250301-8ba, correlation=r=acme-9f3a. Payload (redacted):

```json
{"tools": [
  {"name":"fetch_user","args":{"user_id":12345}},
  {"name":"generate_summary","args":{"doc_id":"d-78a"}}
]}
```

anya: Customer says the response blob for fetch_user was returned with generate_summary's tool_result meta (tool_result.id matched second tool). They saw a schema error on the consumer because generate_summary returns a string summary and fetch_user returns an object.

kevin: Repro attempt: fired two concurrent /v1/call-tool requests with same correlation header. I can repro locally ~30% of runs.
lucas: Stack trace from server side when it misbinds (sanitized):

```
E0301 12:11:05.231 kernel.cpp:482] async_result_map mismatch: correlation r=acme-9f3a
E0301 12:11:05.232 rpc.cpp:119] emitted tool_result for call_id=gen-453 but bound to call_id=fetch-872
E0301 12:11:05.233 schema_validator.cpp:78] expected OBJECT got STRING
```

kevin: Looks like parallel result merging in the callback queue can race when two tools share the same internal batch id. We batch by shard_id and sequence; if internal ids collide we pop the wrong result.
eng-oncall: Thanks — assigning to runtime queue. Mitigation: enable "strict_call_serialization" feature flag for affected customer to force sequential tool dispatch while we patch. Anyone confirmed feature flag toggle works without restart?
anya: Toggled for ACME (org: acme-inc). They reported immediate reduction in failures but still saw one mismatch after toggle (race at the router level?).

lucas: Quick patch idea: add monotonic per-request counter to RPC envelope to avoid depending on batch indices. PR draft: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/812 (WIP). Timeboxed test planned.
kevin: Repro script attached (short curl loop):

```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call-tools \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "X-Correlation-ID: acme-9f3a" \
    -d '{"tools":[{"name":"fetch_user","args":{"user_id":12345}},{"name":"generate_summary","args":{"doc_id":"d-78a"}}]}' &
done
wait
```

billing-bot: Flagged potential double billing: some tool_result retries were recorded as independent invocations. Opening billing investigation BK-122.
eng-oncall: For now recommend: 1) keep strict_call_serialization for ACME, 2) add request-level monotonic counter, 3) patch router to validate tool_result->call_id binding before returning to client (fallback: return 500 to prevent silent misbind).
anya: Customer wants ETA on fix and rollback options. They saw a spike in error counts + two disputed billing line items.
kevin: ETA for hotfix (monotonic counter + validation) ~ 48 hours with tests. If we backport to hosted today we can cut risk in ~6 hours for canary orgs.
lucas: I'll push the validation first (small change) and run unit + stress tests. If green, canary to 5% traffic.
eng-oncall: Create a ticket in runtime repo with logs, repro steps, and affected org list. Tag triage: P1. I'll coordinate on-call rotation for monitoring during canary.
anya: Uploaded sanitized logs and sample payloads to the ticket. Customer notified about temporary serialization and billing review.
kevin: Confirmed repro on infra-qa with the exact loop — attaching trace id set: trace=tr-5521. See attached short trace snippet in the ticket.
eng-oncall: Next actions: patch -> canary -> monitor for 24h -> roll to prod. Billing to reconcile BK-122 and contact customer success.
anya: Thanks all. Please ping me with any blocker. :thumbsup:
